name: Amazon Nova Sonic
access: Amazon Bedrock (legacy; model id amazon.nova-sonic-v1:0; Regions us-east-1, eu-north-1 and ap-northeast-1; new customers cannot adopt a legacy model)

voice.input_audio: Linear PCM (audio/lpcm), 16-bit, mono, base64, at 8,000, 16,000 or 24,000 Hz; the sample code captures 16 kHz [nova1-input-events, nova1-speech-guide]
voice.output_audio: Linear PCM (audio/lpcm), 16-bit, mono, base64, at 8,000, 16,000 or 24,000 Hz; the prompting examples use 24 kHz. AWS marks generated audio with a watermark [nova1-output-events, nova1-service-card]
voice.voices: 11 voice IDs: tiffany, matthew, amy, ambre, florian, beatrice, lorenzo, greta, lennart, lupe and carlos [nova1-voices, nova1-service-card]
voice.turn_detection: Server side. The v1 guide documents no setting to tune it; the endpointingSensitivity setting appears only in the Nova 2 guide [nova1-speech-guide, nova2-sonic-turn-taking]
voice.interruption: Barge-in is supported. The model stops generating, switches to listening and sends a notice, and the client clears its playback queue because audio is generated faster than it plays. The basic Python sample does not implement barge-in [nova1-output-events, nova1-code-examples]
voice.session_limit: An 8-minute connection timeout and up to 20 concurrent connections per customer. The client renews the connection and continues by sending the earlier conversation history in the new request [nova1-model-specs, nova1-errors]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: AWS Price List, Amazon Bedrock, on-demand, US East (N. Virginia), published 2026-10-03. Speech input $0.0034 per 1,000 tokens ($3.40 per million). Speech output $0.0136 per 1,000 ($13.60 per million). Text input $0.06 per million and text output $0.24 per million. Other Regions: eu-north-1 speech $4.10 in and $16.30 out; ap-northeast-1 speech $3.70 in and $14.70 out [aws-price-list].
